gaps: Breath one ran market-births backward, one death per precondition. Three of the brief's pointers refused to be deaths: a copy that takes the liquidity leaves the market alive at another address, a crash leaves it alive at a lower price, and illegality strips the grade, the fence, the witness, and recourse while the trade goes on. What varied across the survivors was what the death left standing for the next market, and the auction-rate failure raised a death by a thing that had never been built, the other side of the auction, which became the changed question for breath two: which deaths refute the belief or the ignorance the next market would need.
accepted: Copy takes the crowd: a market whose lot can be copied exactly at another address dies at the old address on the day the copy holds enough of the crowd that the rest follow for the crowd's sake, as the Bund contract left London's pit for Frankfurt's screen within months once the electronic copy passed its tipping share; the tell is volume falling while open interest holds, since positions are being closed at the old address and opened at the new one; nothing is spent, the market lives at the copy, and the old venue is reborn only by becoming a copy of something else; not a market death so much as the death every other death here is measured against, since it is the one that leaves everything standing.

Sunk into the bundle: a market for a lot dies when deciding whether to buy the lot costs the buyer more than the lot is worth, so the lot is absorbed into a plan and its price survives only as an allocation line, as the ninety-nine-cent song died into the subscription and lives on as a per-stream royalty that no buyer pays; the tell is a price still printed and never paid by a buyer; reversible by unbundling, since the unit still exists inside the plan, and checked bags and airline meals were reborn exactly that way; adjacent to pricing-unit-metamorphoses, which follows the unit through its changes, this names the interval in which the unit has no market at all.

Died into a queue: a market dies by decree of its price when the decree holds the price below what clears, so rationing moves from the price to the line and the market survives as a queue that grows the forbidden sale back as a bribe for a place in it, as rent control breeds key money; the tell is a posted price with a waiting list beside it; reversible by decontrol, but the stock the price was meant to protect has been let rot in the interval and the first free prices are a birth from imported comps, as Cambridge found in 1995; the inverse of market-births' Queue to hijack, which is a market born on a queue, this is a market dying into one.

Slowed past the rot: a market that manufactured its thickness by fixing an hour dies when arrivals fall below what fills the hour, since each seller who leaves lowers the choice a buyer expects and the buyers leave in turn, and the market's last move is to hold the sale less often, weekly then monthly, until the interval passes the shelf life of the lot, as county livestock rings close one by one; the tell is a lengthening interval, not a falling price; reversible by anything that lengthens the shelf life or shortens the distance, as video auctions did for cattle, and the final act is usually a merger with the neighboring ring, so the thin market's death is the copy's birth seen from the losing town.

Wall in one head: where the wall on which offers were compared was one broker's memory, the market dies with the broker's retirement while every buyer and seller still exists, as when the only broker in used presses of one make retires and the holders go back to not knowing each other; the tell is that the market has a telephone number; nothing is spent but the comparison operation, and the market is reborn by any wall, a list, a board, a successor who inherits the notebook; not Hand on the saddle, where the missing thing is the other side, since here both sides are present and only the place they met has died.

Witness starving: a benchmark rests on a physical market whose flow thins until one cargo sets the print for everything indexed to it, as the Brent field declined to a few cargoes a month under contracts worth many times the field; the tell is a single trade moving the month's print, and a party with reason to make that trade; the assessor's cure is to widen the basket, which feeds the witness by changing the lot; not Warm corpse, where the trades have stopped, since here they continue, too few to bear the weight on them.

Warm corpse: a price kept quoted after its trades have stopped because contracts reference it, so the reference keeps the corpse warm, as the interbank term-lending rate was submitted as judgment for a decade after the lending it named had ended, with hundreds of trillions written on it; the tell is that no submitter can name a trade at the print, and the print moves when the panel changes rather than when supply does; rebirth requires a new witness on an underlying that still trades and a statute to move the legacy contracts, since no single party to a contract can leave the corpse alone; not a fraud, which may or may not attend it, but a quote whose only buyer is the contract.

Farm comes back: a grade that let lots substitute fails when its issuer's word stops meaning what it says, so every lot must again be inspected to its own origin, which costs more than the trade, and the market dies not from distrust but from the cost of the inspections distrust demands, as the triple-A on structured paper failed in 2007 and each pool had to be re-underwritten loan by loan; the tell is a bid-ask that widens lot by lot rather than across the board, and buyers asking for the documents behind the grade; rebirth needs a grader with fresh credit rather than a reformed one, since the old grade's memory is poisoned; the reversal of market-births' Grade that erases the farm.

Print taken back: a market dies from the top when the party that made trades final unmakes one, since every later trade is then provisional, as the London Metal Exchange cancelled a morning of nickel trades in March 2022 and the participants who had won the cancelled trades took their volume elsewhere and did not come back; the tell is a rulebook that now shows the power, and a competitor's open interest rising in the same lot; rebirth requires a clearer whose rulebook lacks the power, and the belief in finality is rebuilt one uncancelled crisis at a time; not a default, which is a counterparty failing, but the witness declining to witness.

Fence rots: a lot that was a lot only because a fence was held dies when the fence goes unpoliced, so the lot's price falls while the underlying use goes on, as the New York taxi medallion fell from over a million dollars to a tenth of it while more rides than ever were driven; the tell is the price of the fenced right falling faster than the price of the use; rebirth needs the fence re-held, and the death spends the will to hold it, since the fence's beneficiaries are now a small ruined group and its violators are everyone's drivers; the reversal of market-births' Fence at the lot's edge, which the market could draw but only a state could hold.

Memory set to zero: a market dies when a copy of the good arrives at no price, since the price memory is rewritten to zero and every later price reads as a surcharge on free, as the printed encyclopedia died against the free one and the paid article died against the free page; the tell is paying customers asking why they pay; the memory can be reset only by naming a different lot, membership rather than articles, and news took fifteen years to find one that held; the one death in which nothing is missing and the lot still exists, because what was spent was the number.

One sentence, all holders: a market whose holders all hold for the same reason is one sentence from death, since the sentence failing turns every holder into a seller in the same hour and the price is not low but absent, as money funds held because they never break the buck emptied in the week one broke it; the tell, before the day, is that ten holders asked why they hold give one answer; rebirth comes on a different reason, since the buyers who return are buying distress rather than the thing, so the reborn market has new holders and a new sentence; not a crash, which leaves holders with different reasons on both sides of it.

residue.item: Made illegal: a market dies when the good is banned.
residue.why: Rejected: prohibition strips the grade, the fence, the witness, and recourse, and the trade survives with those gone (spirits over beer because enforcement is per unit, bathtub quality, violence as settlement); it is market-births run backward one precondition at a time, a deformation rather than a death, and its shapes are a map of their own.

residue.item: Crash: the price falls far enough that the market is said to have died.
residue.why: Rejected: a market that clears at a lower price is alive; kept only where the collapse converts every holder into a seller in the same hour (One sentence, all holders) or shows that nobody was ever on the bid, which breath two admitted as Hand on the saddle.

residue.item: Corner: one holder owns the float, so the price is a private number.
residue.why: Rejected: the market is alive at a hostage price for a season; the exchange's response to a corner, liquidation-only orders as in silver in 1980, is Print taken back, and the corner itself is a participant's move rather than a death of the market.

residue.item: Price too costly to send: quoting itself becomes a liability or a burden.
residue.why: Merged into Sunk into the bundle: the brief's pointer split into two carriers, the buyer's cost of deciding per lot, which is the bundle's mechanism, and the seller's cost of posting under most-favored-customer clauses, which kills the wall and moves the trade to whispers; only the first ends the market for the lot.

residue.item: Hyperinflation: prices lose their meaning daily and the shops stop posting them.
residue.why: Held: what dies is the unit of account while the market in bread relocates to dollars, so it may be Copy takes the crowd for money itself rather than a death of the goods market; left as a seed rather than admitted.

gate: declared modality, recognizable distinction, defensible seriation and conditional relations
limits: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not a taxonomy or a partition; a real death usually runs several of these at once (the auction-rate failure was a hand letting go, one sentence held by every holder, and a print with no trades behind it in the same week), and the list makes no claim to cover every way a market ends.

The seriation is an itinerary of what the death leaves standing for the next market, not a ranking of severity, speed, or frequency, and not a prediction of which markets will die; map edges are conditional authored claims.

The illustrative cases (the Bund migration, auction-rate securities, the interbank rate's judgment years, the Brent basket, the 2022 nickel cancellation, New York medallions, the song into the subscription, the Lateran ban, genetic non-discrimination law) are simplified to expose one mechanism each and are not claims about the full histories; the cloud-as-reborn-ice remark inside Question nobody asks is an analogy.

Price collapses, bubbles bursting, corners, and the failure of a participant are outside: a market that clears at a lower or a hostage price is alive. Illegality is also outside as a death, since the fieldwork found that prohibition strips the grade, the fence, the witness, and recourse while the trade survives.
Whether a market should die is outside; Decreed sacred, Died into a queue, and Bid that never blinks describe what a decree does to a market's shape, not whether the decree is right.

gaps: The changed question yielded deaths that spend something an outsider cannot resupply: a buyer who has promised not to refuse and so leaves no memory of a price without it (Bid that never blinks), a question the price no longer answers (Question nobody asks), memory that left in the bodies of the collectors, a belief the death itself refuted (Hand on the saddle), a decree that runs one way (Decreed sacred), and ignorance (Test before the pool). The territory pointer market-deaths stands, but the of-sentence now sorts by what the death leaves standing, and the live question about reversibility resolved into a walk with a hinge at the crossing from what trading remakes to what the death refuted. The first framing looked only for something missing; the new member is a death by something arriving.
accepted: Bid that never blinks: a market dies while quoting when one side stops being able to refuse, as a central bank buying by rule comes to own half the bonds and the benchmark goes a day without a trade, or a dairy support price fills caves with government cheese; the tell is a price that sits on the floor for years and does not move on news, with inventory accumulating at the one buyer; rebirth requires the bid to leave, and when it leaves the market has no memory of a price without it, so the first free prints are a birth; not a monopoly buyer, who refuses at some price, but a buyer who has promised not to.

Question nobody asks: a market dies when a substitute prices the same want in a different unit, so the lot's price stops answering the question buyers ask, as natural ice by the block died against the refrigerator by the machine; the tell is the buyer's question changing unit, per block to per machine, and the market's last customers being those who cannot afford the machine, so the market dies from the top of its customer list; the price is not low but unconsulted, and rebirth comes only when the machine's cost becomes a per-lot price again, as owned servers died back into rented compute, an analogy rather than a history; not Memory set to zero, where the same good arrives free.

Died with the collectors: a market whose price memory lived in its buyers dies when the buyers become estates, so every holder is a seller with no memory and no buyer inherits it, as common stamps and porcelain figurines fell toward material value once the generation that knew their prices was in the ground; the tell is estate in every provenance, dealers' stock growing, and catalogues quoting prices no one pays; no rebirth of that market is possible, since memory kept in people is not resupplied, and a new generation may make a new market on the same objects with its own reason and its own prices; not Memory set to zero, where the number was rewritten, since here the number survives in old catalogues and the rememberers do not.

Hand on the saddle: a market that cleared for twenty years because the sponsor bid in every auction dies on the day the sponsor's hand lets go, and the death is instant because the other side was never there, as auction-rate securities cleared weekly until February 2008 and then failed together; the tell, visible all along, is the same bidder on every print; no rebirth followed, because what the death spent was the buyers' belief that an auction clears by itself, and a belief the death refuted cannot be resupplied by a new sponsor; not Bid that never blinks, where the standing bid is announced and priced, since here the bid was the costume the market wore.

Decreed sacred: a market dies by decree of the good when the community declares it unsaleable, and the transfers do not stop but change kind, moving by gift and by theft, as relics after the Lateran ban travelled by pious theft and organs since 1984 travel by donation chains; the tell is that the gift has a going rate; the death is easy and the reversal nearly impossible, since a good once declared sacred cannot be declared ordinary without the declarer looking like a seller; adjacent to market-births' Price-proof good, a good that payment changes, this is a good that a decree changes, and the asymmetry between the two directions is the finding.

Test before the pool: a market for risk dies when the risk becomes known before the trade, since the pool that priced the unknown dissolves into the certain-loss, who cannot be insured, and the certain-safe, who will not pay, as a genetic test does to a life-insurance pool; the tell is the seller asking for the test; what the death spends is ignorance, which no one can rebuild once the test exists, so rebirth requires a witness built not to see, as genetic non-discrimination law forbids the insurer to ask; the mirror of Farm comes back, which is death by too little known about the lot, this is death by too much.

residue.item: Every buyer their own lot: the seller learns each buyer's price, so no comp exists and no buyer can shop.
residue.why: Rejected: personalized pricing kills the comparison across buyers and leaves the trade, so it is the buyer-side twin of Farm comes back and belongs beside what-a-price-does; kept only where the knowledge kills the trade itself, which is Test before the pool.

residue.item: Paid to stay dead: an incumbent pays the substitute to stay off the market.
residue.why: Rejected: pay-for-delay prevents a birth rather than causing a death, and belongs beside first-mover-forecloses.

residue.item: Pious theft: after the ban, theft becomes the licit way a relic changes hands.
residue.why: Merged into Decreed sacred as the tell that transfers change kind rather than stopping; on its own it is a case, not a second mechanism.

residue.item: Cloud as reborn ice: rented compute is the per-lot market for cold returning after decades of owned machines.
residue.why: Kept as a marked analogy inside Question nobody asks rather than as an item; the mechanism it points at, per-lot beating capital when utilization is low, is the rebirth condition for that item, not a death.

residue.item: Unit of account dies: hyperinflation with every other precondition intact.
residue.why: Unresolved seed: Hyperinflation as a death of the unit of account with every other precondition intact: is the goods market dead, or relocated as Copy takes the crowd for money, and does the relocation carry the price memory across at a conversion rate or set it to nothing?

neighbors.left: Memory set to zero: a market dies when a copy of the good arrives at no price, since the price memory is rewritten to zero and every later price reads as a surcharge on free, as the printed encyclopedia died against the free one and the paid article died against the free page; the tell is paying customers asking why they pay; the memory can be reset only by naming a different lot, membership rather than articles, and news took fifteen years to find one that held; the one death in which nothing is missing and the lot still exists, because what was spent was the number.

neighbors.separating_case: Sheet music after free scores went online: the memory of the music's price was rewritten to zero while the collectors of first editions remained, and their market lived on with its prices. Porcelain figurines: nothing ever became free, the catalogues still print the old prices, and the buyers left with the memory in them. The first is a number rewritten with the rememberers present; the second is the rememberers gone with the number intact, and only the first can be reseeded by renaming the lot.

checks.boundary_case: A price collapse is out: the oil price halved across 2014 and 2016 and the market cleared every day, so it was alive at a lower price. It comes in only where the collapse converts every holder into a seller in the same hour, which is One sentence, all holders, or reveals that nobody was ever on the bid, which is Hand on the saddle. Prohibition is out for the opposite reason: the trade survives with its grade, fence, and witness stripped, which is a deformation, not a death.
checks.form_inference: The map shows a fork the sequence conceals at Witness starving, which the itinerary places once but which splits by whether a substitute field exists: fed, it drifts into Farm comes back; unfed, it dies into Warm corpse. It shows an incompatibility at the limits between Farm comes back and Test before the pool, the same variable, how much is known about the lot, killing the market at too little and again at too much, so a risk market lives only inside a band of ignorance. It shows a dependency at Bid that never blinks → One sentence, all holders, where the floor manufactures the run that follows its removal, two deaths in sequence from one cause. It shows a passage between levels at Sunk into the bundle → Memory set to zero, where the most reversible death ripens into an irreversible one from inside. It shows a second dependency at Decreed sacred → Died into a queue, where the sacred recruits the queue and the queue recruits the sale. And it shows that Print taken back kills only when Copy takes the crowd is available, the two ends of the itinerary joined by an edge the line cannot draw.
checks.target_preserved: Self-read only. Each admitted item names a distinct carrier of the death, a distinct tell visible while the market still quotes, and a distinct answer to what a rebirth needs; the strange members (a corpse kept warm by contracts, a bicycle held up by a hand on the saddle, a death by too much knowledge, a good that moves by pious theft once it cannot be sold) are kept as mechanisms rather than softened into warnings about market risk.

next_crossfield_opening: Deaths by knowledge: connect Test before the pool with witness-architectures' Blindfolded tally and market-births' Grade that erases the farm; ask which markets exist only inside a band of ignorance, and whether a witness built not to see can hold such a market open after the test exists or can only delay its death.

gaps: The map's own boundary rule (a market clearing at a lower or hostage price is alive) killed two members as written: Fence rots was a crash of a fenced right still trading at a tenth, and Witness starving was the condition before a death, with a tell and a cure but no death and no rebirth. Behind that, three illustrative cases were asserted as history and were wrong or overclaimed: the American genetic non-discrimination statute leaves life cover outside; nickel volume at the venue came back after two years, as the map's own edge predicted for a cancellation without a copy; the revived structured-credit markets were rated by the same agencies under a new rule.

Fence rots: a lot that was a lot only because a fence was held dies when the fence goes unpoliced enough that the fenced right trades at the price of its paperwork while the underlying use goes on, as the New York taxi medallion fell from over a million dollars toward a tenth of it while more rides than ever were driven, a death still in progress since the fence is half held and the medallion half priced; the tell is the price of the fenced right falling faster than the price of the use, and the death is complete when the two no longer move together at all; rebirth needs the fence re-held, and the death spends the will to hold it, since the fence's beneficiaries are now a small ruined group and its violators are everyone's drivers; the reversal of market-births' Fence at the lot's edge, which the market could draw but only a state could hold, and not a crash of the right, which is a fence still held at a lower rent.

Farm comes back: a grade that let lots substitute fails when its issuer's word stops meaning what it says, so every lot must again be inspected to its own origin, which costs more than the trade, and the market dies not from distrust but from the cost of the inspections distrust demands, as the triple-A on structured paper failed in 2007 and each pool had to be re-underwritten loan by loan; the tell is a bid-ask that widens lot by lot rather than across the board, and buyers asking for the documents behind the grade; rebirth needs the grade's word re-credited, by a new grader or by the old one under a new rule, and in structured credit the old graders kept the job under risk retention, so what was re-credited was the rule and not the name; the reversal of market-births' Grade that erases the farm.

Copy takes the crowd: a market whose lot can be copied exactly at another address dies at the old address on the day the copy holds enough of the crowd that the rest follow for the crowd's sake, as the Bund contract left London's pit for Frankfurt's screen within a year once the electronic copy passed its tipping share; the tell is volume falling while open interest holds, since positions are being closed at the old address and opened at the new one; nothing is spent, the market lives at the copy, and the old venue is reborn only by becoming a copy of something else; not a market death so much as the death every other death here is measured against, since it is the one that leaves everything standing.

limits: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not a taxonomy or a partition; a real death usually runs several of these at once (the auction-rate failure was a hand letting go, one sentence held by every holder, and a print with no trades behind it in the same week), and the list makes no claim to cover every way a market ends. The word market is used loosely across the items, sometimes for a venue (Copy takes the crowd) and sometimes for a lot (Sunk into the bundle); the map tolerates the looseness rather than resolving it.

Price collapses, bubbles bursting, corners, and the failure of a participant are outside: a market that clears at a lower or a hostage price is alive. The lot itself ceasing to exist, as when the last lab that processed a film closed, is outside, since the good died and not the market; every admitted item has the lot's use surviving the market's death. Illegality is also outside as a death, since the fieldwork found that prohibition strips the grade, the fence, the witness, and recourse while the trade survives.
seed: The edge Print taken back → Copy takes the crowd contains a second axis the map does not draw: whether a copy of the lot exists decides, for that death, whether the event kills or only deforms. The same variable runs under Wall in one head (a successor's notebook is a copy of the wall), Slowed past the rot (the neighboring ring), and Warm corpse (an underlying that still trades is a copy of the witness's subject), and it is what separates the map's deaths from the ledger's rejected deformations (prohibition, corner, crash). A map of the same eighteen deaths sorted by copy-with and copy-without would show which deaths are deaths at all only in a world with one address, and whether the four irreversible deaths at the end are irreversible because no copy of a belief or an ignorance can exist.
